title: Order-to-Cash
subtitle: From customer order to cash collection, documented as a functional design
thesis: One order. One delivery. One invoice. One payment that can be traced.
role: Process analysis, requirements, fit-gap, functional design, test and migration planning
status: Document set only — no ERP configured, no test executed, no data migrated
typeLabel: Independent learning case study, fictional scenario
boundary: PT Sinar Distribusi Nusantara is a fictional company created for this exercise. The process, rules and requirements are designed to demonstrate analysis, not to describe a real client. No ERP product was configured, no customer or supplier was contacted, no transaction was executed, and no business outcome is claimed.
summary: An independent learning case study: one process, taken from customer order through validation, availability, approval, fulfilment, delivery, billing and cash application, documented as rules, requirements and testable acceptance criteria.

context.company: PT Sinar Distribusi Nusantara (fictional), a wholesale distributor of packaged consumer and industrial products.
context.situation: Commercial activity runs on spreadsheets, email and separate departmental records. Sales confirms orders without a reliable stock view, and warehouse, logistics and finance each keep their own copy of what happened.
context.problem: A single order can be recorded differently by sales, warehouse, logistics and finance. Reconstructing what was ordered, delivered and invoiced means assembling evidence from four functions, so the invoice is only as reliable as the folder it came from.
context.why: One document chain — order, delivery, invoice, payment — makes the commitment traceable and gives each role one place to see what it owns.

stakeholders.responsibility: Creates and maintains customer orders, and answers the customer on order status.
stakeholders.interaction: Enters the order in Draft and hands it to validation; cannot release stock or approve credit.

stakeholders.responsibility: Approves or rejects commercial exceptions within an authority band.
stakeholders.interaction: Approves, rejects or escalates; cannot approve an order outside the band or their own request.

stakeholders.responsibility: Owns customer and product master records.
stakeholders.interaction: Creates, changes and deactivates records; resolves potential duplicates before they spread.

stakeholders.responsibility: Owns stock accuracy and the availability commitment.
stakeholders.interaction: Confirms available-to-promise and reservations before an order is released.

stakeholders.responsibility: Picks, packs and records goods issue.
stakeholders.interaction: Records picked and packed quantities against a released order.

stakeholders.responsibility: Executes delivery and captures proof of delivery.
stakeholders.interaction: Records delivery status, proof of delivery and the reason for a failed attempt.

stakeholders.responsibility: Creates invoices, records payments and allocates cash.
stakeholders.interaction: Cannot authorise a credit release, a return or a write-off.

stakeholders.responsibility: Owns credit policy, receivables control and financial exceptions.
stakeholders.interaction: Releases credit blocks, authorises returns and approves write-offs with a recorded reason.

stakeholders.responsibility: Sets direction, reviews performance and approves go/no-go.
stakeholders.interaction: Reviews consolidated KPIs and control exceptions; does not transact.

process.heading: Order to cash, in ten stages

steps.name: Maintain master data
steps.decision: Unique ID and mandatory fields satisfied?

steps.name: Create sales order
steps.output: Order in Draft with customer, products and price.
steps.decision: Active customer and product, price found?

steps.name: Validate order
steps.output: Order Validated or returned to Draft.
steps.decision: Mandatory fields and reference data complete?

steps.name: Credit and approval check
steps.output: Approved and released, on hold, or rejected.
steps.decision: Within credit limit and approval band?

steps.name: Release and fulfil
steps.output: Picked and packed quantities against the order.

steps.name: Create customer invoice
steps.output: Posted invoice linked to the delivery and order.
steps.decision: Billing trigger, price and statutory data agree?

steps.name: Record and allocate payment
steps.output: Allocated payment and visible unapplied cash.

steps.name: Monitor receivables and report
steps.decision: Cut-off rules and KPI definitions applied?

exceptions: Insufficient stock offers a backorder, split delivery or reschedule, and the customer decision is recorded (EX-03).
A rejected or credit-held order cannot be released; Finance records the release reason and timestamp (EX-04, EX-05).
An invoice is created only from a confirmed proof of delivery; a second billing run for the same delivery is blocked (AC-09, AC-10).
A return references the original delivery and invoice, and the requester cannot authorise it (EX-08, BR-12).

rules.rule: Every customer and product must have a unique master-data identifier.
Invalid mandatory customer or product information shall prevent order confirmation.
Inventory availability must be checked before confirming a delivery commitment.
Order approval thresholds must follow an authorised business policy.
Fulfilment quantities must follow approved partial or over-delivery rules.
Invoice creation must follow an approved billing trigger.
Payment allocation must remain traceable to the relevant customer and invoice.
Users may only access transactions permitted by their assigned roles.
An order that exceeds the approved credit limit is blocked from release until Finance releases it with a reason and timestamp.
An invoice cannot be created before delivery is confirmed by proof of delivery; no proof, no invoice.
A manual price override above the agreed tolerance requires Sales Manager approval and a recorded reason.
A return must reference the original delivery and invoice and carry a reason code; the requester cannot authorise it.
Master data is deactivated, never deleted; change history is retained for audit.
Over-delivery is not permitted without approval; partial delivery is permitted and leaves the remainder open.
A posted invoice is never edited or deleted; corrections use credit or debit notes that reference the original.

requirements.title: Customer master records
requirements.description: The system shall maintain customer master records with unique identifiers.
requirements.behavior: A duplicate tax ID is blocked, the possible duplicate is shown, and no second record is saved (AC-01).

requirements.title: Product master records
requirements.description: The system shall maintain product master records with unique identifiers, descriptions, and units of measure.
requirements.behavior: A duplicate product code is blocked and the conflicting product is named (AC-02).

requirements.title: Create and update sales orders
requirements.description: Authorised Sales users shall be able to create and update sales orders.
requirements.behavior: Only permitted fields change and each change writes an audit entry (AC-03); an unauthorised user is denied and the event logged (AC-04).

requirements.title: Validate order data
requirements.description: The system shall validate customer, product, quantity, and required order fields.
requirements.behavior: Confirmation is blocked, the missing field is named, and the order stays Draft (AC-05).

requirements.title: Inventory availability information
requirements.description: The system shall provide inventory availability information during order processing.
requirements.behavior: Available-to-promise shows on-hand minus reservations; an over-commit needs an exception (AC-06).

requirements.title: Configurable approval rules
requirements.description: The system shall support configurable order approval rules.
requirements.behavior: Approval bands route an order to the correct approver and record the decision.

requirements.title: Generate fulfilment requirements
requirements.description: The system shall generate fulfilment requirements from eligible confirmed orders.
requirements.behavior: A second release creates no second fulfilment requirement and the attempt is logged (AC-07).

requirements.title: Record picked, packed and shipped quantities
requirements.description: The system shall record picked, packed, and shipped quantities.
requirements.behavior: Over-delivery is rejected unless an approved tolerance or reason is recorded (AC-08).

requirements.title: Delivery status and evidence
requirements.description: The system shall record delivery status and supporting evidence where applicable.
requirements.behavior: Delivery status and proof of delivery are visible against the order.

requirements.title: Invoice from an approved trigger
requirements.description: The system shall support customer invoice creation based on an approved billing trigger.
requirements.behavior: One delivery produces exactly one invoice (AC-09); a repeat billing run creates none (AC-10).

requirements.title: Invoice status tracking
requirements.description: The system shall track invoice statuses, including open, partially paid, and cleared.
requirements.behavior: A partial payment moves the invoice to Partially Paid; full payment clears it (AC-11).

requirements.title: Record and allocate payments
requirements.description: The system shall support recording and allocation of incoming payments.
requirements.behavior: Unallocated cash stays visible (AC-12); an allocation above the payment is refused (AC-13).

requirements.title: End-to-end document traceability
requirements.description: The system shall maintain traceability between sales orders, fulfilment, deliveries, invoices, and payments.
requirements.behavior: Every child document is reachable in both directions and no orphan document exists (AC-14).

requirements.title: Operational reporting
requirements.description: The system shall provide operational reports for orders, fulfilment, billing, and receivables.
requirements.behavior: Two reports for the same period use one KPI definition and agree.

requirements.title: Transaction history for audit
requirements.description: The system shall maintain transaction history for audit purposes.
requirements.behavior: User, timestamp, action and reason are visible and cannot be edited (AC-15).

requirements.title: Returns and credit notes
requirements.description: The system shall support customer returns and credit notes linked to the original delivery and invoice, with an authorisation step separate from the request.
requirements.behavior: The requester cannot authorise their own return (AC-16); an accepted return posts a credit note and reduces the receivable (AC-17).

requirements.title: Credit exposure check
requirements.description: The system shall evaluate customer credit exposure at order confirmation and block or route orders that exceed the approved credit limit.
requirements.behavior: An over-limit order is blocked or routed to Finance; release needs a reason and timestamp (AC-18).

requirements.title: Backorder and outstanding quantity
requirements.description: The system shall record outstanding order quantities and support backorder release when stock becomes available.
requirements.behavior: The remainder stays open after a partial fulfilment and is released when stock arrives.

requirements.title: Price determination and override control
requirements.description: The system shall determine order and invoice prices from maintained price conditions and record any manual override with approval and reason.
requirements.behavior: An unapproved override is refused until an authorised approver records a reason (AC-19).

requirements.title: Lifecycle status and valid transitions
requirements.description: The system shall expose a defined lifecycle status for orders, deliveries, invoices, payments, and returns, and permit only valid transitions.
requirements.behavior: A closed order cannot move back to Released; the attempt is logged (AC-20).

requirements.title: Exception register
requirements.description: The system shall record order and delivery exceptions with reason code, owner, timestamp, and resolution.
requirements.behavior: Each exception has a named owner and a recorded resolution.

requirements.title: Statutory invoice data
requirements.description: The system shall store and output statutory invoice data determined by Finance-configured rules.
requirements.behavior: Tax identifier, amount, number and date reconcile on output (AC-21); missing configuration blocks posting (AC-22).

requirements.title: Duplicate detection at master data entry
requirements.description: The system shall detect potential duplicate customer and product records at entry using defined matching attributes.
requirements.behavior: A likely duplicate is shown before the record is saved.

acceptance.given: A customer record already exists with a tax ID
acceptance.when: A user creates a customer with the same tax ID
acceptance.then: Creation is blocked, the possible duplicate is shown, and no second record is saved

acceptance.given: A product exists with code P-100 and unit CTN
acceptance.when: A user creates another product with code P-100
acceptance.then: Creation is blocked and the conflicting product is named

acceptance.given: An authorised Sales user is signed in
acceptance.when: They create and update an order
acceptance.then: Only permitted fields change, and each change writes an audit entry

acceptance.given: A user without the Sales order role is signed in
acceptance.when: They attempt to create an order
acceptance.then: The action is denied and a security event is recorded

acceptance.given: An order is in Draft
acceptance.when: The user confirms it with a missing mandatory field or inactive product
acceptance.then: Confirmation is blocked, the field is named, and the order stays Draft

acceptance.given: Stock on hand is 100 and 30 are reserved
acceptance.when: A user enters an order line for 80
acceptance.then: Available-to-promise shows 70 and the order cannot commit 80 without an exception

acceptance.given: An order has been released to the warehouse
acceptance.when: A user attempts to release it a second time
acceptance.then: No second fulfilment requirement is created and the attempt is logged

acceptance.given: An order line is for 10 units with 0% over-delivery tolerance
acceptance.when: The operator records 12 picked
acceptance.then: The system rejects the excess unless an approved tolerance or reason is recorded

acceptance.given: A delivery is POD Confirmed
acceptance.when: The billing run processes that delivery
acceptance.then: Exactly one invoice is created, referencing the delivery and order

acceptance.given: An invoice already exists for a delivery
acceptance.when: The billing run processes the same delivery again
acceptance.then: No second invoice is created and the duplicate attempt is logged

acceptance.given: An invoice for 1,000 is Open
acceptance.when: A payment of 400 is allocated to it
acceptance.then: Status becomes Partially Paid; after 600 more, status becomes Cleared

acceptance.given: A payment of 1,000 is recorded
acceptance.when: The user allocates 600 to one invoice and 300 to another
acceptance.then: The payment stays Partially Allocated and 100 remains visible as unapplied cash

acceptance.given: A payment of 1,000 is recorded
acceptance.when: A user attempts to allocate 1,100
acceptance.then: Allocation is rejected because it exceeds the payment amount

acceptance.given: An order has a delivery, invoice, and payment
acceptance.when: A user traces the order
acceptance.then: All child documents are reachable in both directions and no orphan document exists

acceptance.given: Any transaction has been created or changed
acceptance.when: An auditor opens its history
acceptance.then: User, timestamp, action, and reason (where required) are visible and cannot be edited

acceptance.given: A return is requested
acceptance.when: The same user attempts to authorise it
acceptance.then: Authorisation is refused; a different authorised role must decide

acceptance.given: Goods are returned against a valid delivery and invoice
acceptance.when: The goods are received and accepted
acceptance.then: A credit note is created, referencing both, and the receivable balance reduces

acceptance.given: A customer's exposure exceeds the approved credit limit
acceptance.when: A Sales user confirms an order
acceptance.then: The order is blocked or routed to Finance; release requires a Finance decision with reason and timestamp

acceptance.given: A product has a maintained price of 100
acceptance.when: A user overrides the price to 90 without approval
acceptance.then: The override is refused until an authorised approver records a reason

acceptance.given: An order is Closed
acceptance.when: A user attempts to move it back to Released
acceptance.then: The transition is refused and the attempt is logged

acceptance.given: Statutory invoice configuration is complete
acceptance.when: An invoice is posted and printed
acceptance.then: Tax identifier, tax amount, invoice number, and invoice date are present and reconcile

acceptance.given: Statutory invoice configuration is missing a required element
acceptance.when: A user attempts to post an invoice
acceptance.then: Posting is blocked and the missing configuration is named

exceptions.scenario: Incomplete, invalid, or duplicate customer or product master record
exceptions.expected: Block creation; return with a field-level reason; duplicate resolution is required.
Block confirmation; the order returns to Draft with errors listed per field.
Offer backorder, split delivery or reschedule; record the customer decision.
Record the rejection reason, notify Sales, and keep the order unreleased.

exceptions.scenario: Credit limit exceeded or payment overdue
exceptions.expected: Hold the order; Finance reviews exposure and releases or rejects with reason and timestamp.
Ship the available quantity, backorder the remainder, and inform the customer of the revised date.
Record reason and evidence; reschedule, reattempt or return the goods to the warehouse.
Do not ship, or start the return flow R1; record evidence.
Keep as unapplied cash; AR investigates; any adjustment requires approval.
Collection follow-up, credit hold per policy, and escalation.
Hold the invoice and correct it before posting; after posting, use a credit or debit note, never edit.
Warn Sales; link or cancel the duplicate and record the decision.
Deny the action, record a security event, and notify IT.

exceptions.scenario: Master data changed after transactions exist
exceptions.expected: Permit a controlled change, retain history, and revalidate affected open documents.
Record the substitution and customer consent, then adjust the order line before picking.

erp.note: Order, delivery, invoice and payment are linked documents, not free-standing records. Each child references its parent (FR-13).
Customer, product and warehouse records exist before a transaction. An order cannot reference a customer or product that is not master data (BR-01).
Each document carries a status and only defined transitions are allowed (FR-20). A closed order cannot be reopened.
Order entry, approval, fulfilment, billing and cash allocation are separate roles, not one administrator account (BR-08).
Approval depends on a value band, and the decision records who approved, when, and why (BR-04, FR-06).
Credit exposure is checked before release; Finance, not Sales, releases a block (BR-09, FR-17).
Availability, reservation and goods issue change stock. Releasing the same order twice would corrupt the commitment (FR-05, FR-07).
The posted invoice becomes a receivable; payment allocation closes it and posts to the ledger (FR-10 to FR-12).
Every state change keeps actor, time and previous state so a paid invoice can be explained later (FR-15).

in: One company, one currency and one order-to-cash boundary.
Customer order through validation, availability, approval, fulfilment, delivery, billing and cash application.
Returns and credit notes as a proposed reverse flow.
Master data, role design, controls, UAT planning and migration planning.
out: Manufacturing, procurement, general ledger, HR and fixed assets.
A specific ERP product, edition or licence configuration.
Real bank, carrier, WMS or tax/e-invoice connectivity.
Benefit quantification or return on investment.
limits: PT Sinar Distribusi Nusantara is fictional; the problems are illustrative, not field research.
No ERP product was validated; every fit classification is a hypothesis.
No test was executed, no data migrated and no cutover was performed.
No policy is approved; approval bands, credit limits and the billing trigger remain open questions.
No measured outcome, time saving or cost reduction is claimed.
